title: Crystal Grid — Apple-Keynote Feature Bento
description: Five rounded, glassy tiles — one dominant 2×2 hero flanked by four 1×1 feature cells — built to reveal product strengths the way Apple does: one icon, one phrase, nothing more. The soft inner highlight gradient keeps each tile tactile without competing with its content.
philosophy: This template exists for the moment when a product's strengths must land in parallel and instantly. It refuses body copy, competing typographic hierarchies, and decorative fills that upstage the hardware. The grid itself makes the argument: asymmetry lives only in tile scale, never in craftsmanship. It is designed for rooms where the slide appears on a high-resolution display and must hold its own against the object it describes.
goodFor: Hardware or software product feature reveals at keynote scale
Tech startup pitch decks showcasing exactly five differentiators
One-icon-per-benefit storytelling on large projected displays
Apple-ecosystem product pages adapted into slide format
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly reviews requiring multiple data series per slide
Academic content needing citations, captions, and dense body paragraphs
Decks with more than five discrete features requiring simultaneous display
Warm, rustic, or hand-crafted brand identities
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide captures the hushed moment before a product reveal — cool luminosity, one glassy plane commanding the stage. A dominant frosted-glass hero tile anchors the center while ghost-outlines of the flanking bento cells dissolve off the edges, teasing the grid that follows. Mood is Cupertino-restrained and Nordic-cool: precision without sterility, tactile without ornament. Avoid competing gradient fills and any compositional rigidity that reads formal or corporate rather than editorial and inevitable.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with 6% outer margins and no header band. A single oversized frosted-glass hero tile spans columns 2–11 and sits vertically centered at roughly the upper 45% of the slide, acting as the full compositional stage for the title and subtitle. Four smaller tile ghost-shapes are clipped at the slide corners to imply the bento grid waiting in the deck, without competing for attention. Hierarchy is carried by scale contrast alone — title anchored inside the hero tile, subtitle set below with generous vertical breathing room; no page number on the cover.

examples.promptCore: Apple Keynote product-reveal energy — tactile yet weightless, like precision hardware resting on a matte stage. Each frosted-glass tile breathes with a soft inner highlight that implies depth without decoration; the hero tile commands attention through sheer scale, never through loudness. The four satellite cells answer it in composed symmetry, each whispering a single differentiator through icon and short phrase alone. Avoid competing gradients, ornamental fills, or any typographic layering that disrupts the deliberate stillness of the grid.

examples.layoutNotes: Twelve-column grid with roughly 6% outer margin on all sides; the hero tile occupies the left seven columns at full content-row height while the four 1×1 satellite cells fill the remaining right band in a 2×2 sub-grid. Each tile is a self-contained rounded rectangle — hierarchy is established entirely by tile footprint, never by internal borders or rule lines. A single icon sits centered in the upper portion of each tile with a one-line label anchored below it; no header band is used, and only a discreet folio mark appears at the bottom-right corner outside the grid.
